<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[2023 DRC anti-MONUSCO protests]]
***At least 48 people are killed during a crackdown on anti-[[United Nations]] protests in [[Goma]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/africa/1693551114-deadly-crackdown-on-anti-un-protest-in-dr-congo-s-east (i24 NEWS)]
* [[2023 Gabonese coup d'état]]
**Officers of the [[Gabon]]ese [[Armed Forces of Gabon|military]] depose [[President of Gabon|president]] [[Ali Bongo Ondimba|Ali Bongo]] and annul the results of the [[2023 Gabonese general election|general election]] in which Bongo was declared the winner. They also dissolve the [[politics of Gabon|government]] and close all borders. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gabonese-military-officers-announce-they-have-seized-power-2023-08-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Bombing of Kyiv]]
***Two people are killed and three others are injured in a [[Russia]]n [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] and missile strike on [[Kyiv]]. [[Ukraine]] says that it shot down several missiles and drones during the strike. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/explosions-heard-ukraines-kyiv-mayor-2023-08-30/ (Reuters)]
**[[Ministry of Defense (Russia)|Russia]] says that its aircraft destroyed four military boats carrying up to 50 members from [[Beach groups|landing groups]] of the [[special forces of Ukraine]] operating in the [[Black Sea]] as well as two [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|military]] speedboats carrying military personnel east of [[Snake Island (Ukraine)|Snake Island]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/30/russia-claims-ukrainian-special-forces-boats-destroyed-in-black-sea (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-says-its-forces-destroyed-us-made-military-vessel-near-snake-island-2023-08-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Rojava conflict]]
***Clashes in [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate|Deir ez-Zor]] between [[Bedouin|Arab tribal]] fighters and [[Kurds|Kurdish]]-led fighters kill and injure several people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/8/30/several-killed-in-fighting-between-sdf-and-tribesmen-in-eastern-syria (Al Jazeera)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022–2023 Russia–European Union gas dispute]]
***[[Global Witness]] reveals that [[EU countries|EU]] countries increased their imports of [[liquefied natural gas]] from [[Russia]] despite committing to reductions, rising by 40% in 2023, accounting for 22 million cubic meters. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/lng-imports-russia-rise-despite-cuts-pipeline-gas-2023-08-30/ (Reuters)]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Economic sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[India]] asks the [[United States]] to release $26m belonging to at least two Indian diamond firms that has been [[Asset freezing|frozen]] due to alleged trade links with [[Office of Foreign Assets Control|sanctioned]] Russian [[List of diamond mines|diamond mining]] company [[Alrosa]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india-asks-us-release-funds-frozen-over-suspected-russia-diamond-link-sources-2023-08-30/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Idalia]] makes landfall in the [[U.S. state]] of [[Florida]] as a [[Saffir–Simpson scale#Category 3|category 3]] [[hurricane]]. Flooding is reported in the [[Tampa Bay area]], including [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]] and other parts of [[Hillsborough County, Florida|Hillsborough County]]. Two deaths are reported with both being due to [[traffic collision|vehicle accidents]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/weather/2023/08/30/hurricane-idalia-landfall-florida-live-updates/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://spotonflorida.com/west-central-florida/4803288/hurricane-idalia-flooding-in-tampa-and-hillsborough.html (Spot On Florida)]
*The death toll from torrential rains in [[Tajikistan]] increase to 21, as flooding, [[landslide]]s, and [[mudflow]]s affect towns near [[Dushanbe]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/toll-from-heavy-rains-in-tajikistan-rises-to-21-d29f1b8a (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Russia and the United Nations|Russia]] [[United Nations Security Council veto power|vetoes]] a [[United Nations Security Council]] [[United Nations resolution|resolution]] to extend targeted [[Economic sanctions|sanctions]] on [[Mali]] for one year and maintain a team of [[United Nations special rapporteur|UN rapporteurs]] investigating [[Human rights in Mali|abuses]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230831-russia-vetoes-un-resolution-on-mali-sanctions (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Former [[National Army of Colombia|Colombian National Army General]] [[Mario Montoya Uribe]] is charged for his role in the [["false positives" scandal]]. Montoya is accused of carrying out [[Extrajudicial killing|extrajudicial executions]] of 130 people. [https://www.laprensalatina.com/jep-charges-former-army-commander-with-false-positives-for-first-time/ (La Prensa Latina)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Australian Indigenous Voice referendum]]
**[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Anthony Albanese]] announces that the Australian Indigenous Voice referendum will be held on 14 October. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-08-30/voice-to-parliament-referendum-date-set-october-14/102757140 (ABC News)]
*[[2023 Guatemalan general election]]
**[[List of presidents of the Congress of the Republic of Guatemala|President of Congress]] [[Shirley Rivera]] dissolves the parliamentary group of [[Semilla (political party)|Movimiento Semilla]] and declares them "[[Independent politician|independent]]". President-elect and member of Congress [[Bernardo Arévalo]] is also affected by the decision. [https://lahora.gt/nacionales/la-hora/2023/08/30/siguen-las-consecuencias-del-resultado-electoral-congreso-desconoce-a-la-bacada-semilla/ (''La Hora'')]
*[[2024 Mexican general election]]
**The [[Broad Front for Mexico]] fields [[LXIV Legislature of the Mexican Congress|Senator]] [[Xóchitl Gálvez]] as its candidate for [[President of Mexico|president]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20230831-mexico-opposition-picks-businesswoman-galvez-as-presidential-candidate (AFP via RFI)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship of TikTok]]
**[[Kyrgyzstan]]'s [[Ministry of Culture, Information, Sports and Youth Policy (Kyrgyzstan)|Ministry of Culture, Information, Sports and Youth Policy]] announces that it will ban the [[TikTok]] platform in an effort to protect the health of young children. [https://www.rferl.org/a/kyrgyzstan-tiktok-ban-children/32571122.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 in volleyball]]
** In an event billed as "[[Volleyball Day in Nebraska]]", 92,003 people fill the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]]'s [[Memorial Stadium (Lincoln)|Memorial Stadium]] for a match between the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers women's volleyball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] and [[Omaha Mavericks]], setting a new verified attendance record for a women's sports event. [https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/38294591/nebraska-volleyball-sets-world-record-attendance-women-sporting-event (ESPN)]
